topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 4 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the minimum age to drive a motor cycle without gear with engine capacity not exceeding 50 cc is:
e: The general minimum age is 18 years, but a person who has completed 16 years may drive a gearless motor cycle of up to 50 cc with the consent of the guardian.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, in the case of a vehicle subject to a hire-purchase, lease or hypothecation agreement, the 'owner' means:
o: The manufacturer until the loan is repaid
The person in possession of the vehicle under that agreement
e: The Act treats the person in possession under a hire-purchase, lease or hypothecation agreement as the owner, which is why the hirer is the insured and liable for third party claims.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under the Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025 framed under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, a victim is entitled to cashless treatment up to:
e: The scheme, notified by MoRTH in 2025, provides cashless treatment up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for a maximum of seven days from the date of accident at designated hospitals, funded through the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 194 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), the penalty for driving an overloaded goods vehicle is:
e: The amended Section 194 prescribes a minimum fine of ₹20,000 together with ₹2,000 for every additional tonne of excess load. Overloading also affects OD claim settlement under non-standard claim guidelines.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Which of the following best states the ratio of Skandia Insurance Co. v. Kokilaben Chandravadan (1987)?
o: The insurer can escape liability only if the breach of the driver's licence condition was wilful on the part of the insured
An insurer can avoid liability for any breach of policy condition by the insured
Third parties cannot claim against the insurer directly
Gratuitous passengers are covered under Act policies
e: The Supreme Court held that the breach must be wilful: where the owner handed the vehicle to a licensed driver who let an unlicensed person drive without the owner's knowledge, the insurer remained liable.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 145 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the term 'third party' includes:
e: Section 145(g) expressly provides that 'third party' includes the Government, so damage to public property such as electricity poles or road dividers is a third party property damage claim.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 134 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident causing injury must:
o: Leave the scene to avoid a mob
Inform the insurer before the police
Take reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured and report to the nearest police station within 24 hours
e: Section 134 imposes a duty on the driver/person in charge to secure medical attention for the injured, convey them to the nearest hospital unless impracticable, and report the accident to the police within 24 hours.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Under the compulsory personal accident cover for owner-driver, the capital sum insured currently is:
e: IRDAI raised the CPA cover for owner-driver to ₹15 lakh from January 2019 (earlier ₹2 lakh for private cars and ₹1 lakh for two-wheelers), at an annual premium of ₹750.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Under the owner-driver PA cover, loss of one limb or sight of one eye entitles the insured to:
e: The scale of compensation is 100% for death, loss of two limbs or sight of both eyes (or one limb and one eye) and permanent total disablement, and 50% for loss of one limb or sight of one eye.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), the no-fault compensation payable in case of death of a victim is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 164 provides ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt without the claimant having to prove negligence. It replaced the earlier Section 140 (₹50,000 / ₹25,000) and Section 163A.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: An insured already holds a personal accident policy of ₹20 lakh. On buying a new two-wheeler, is the compulsory PA cover for owner-driver required?
o: Yes, but only for 50% of the sum insured
No, as IRDAI permits waiver where the owner-driver holds a general PA cover of at least ₹15 lakh
e: IRDAI's January 2019 circular allows an owner-driver with an existing PA cover of ₹15 lakh or more to be exempted from the compulsory PA cover under the motor policy.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: A passenger carrying commercial vehicle for motor insurance purposes includes all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Dumpers fall under miscellaneous and special type vehicles. Taxis, auto rickshaws, e-rickshaws and buses are passenger carrying vehicles, rated on seating capacity.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: A 'contract carriage' under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a vehicle that:
o: Is engaged as a whole for carriage of passengers under a contract for a fixed sum, with no stops to pick up other passengers
Carries passengers at separate fares for stages of a journey
Carries goods under a written contract
Is used only within municipal limits
e: Section 2(7) defines a contract carriage as a vehicle engaged under a contract for the whole vehicle for a fixed or agreed rate, as distinct from a stage carriage that charges individual fares.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Under the 2022 third party premium notification, electric private cars receive a discount on TP premium of:
e: The notification grants a 15% discount on TP premium for electric vehicles and 7.5% for hybrid electric vehicles, to encourage adoption of clean vehicles.

topic: Underwriting and Rating
t: A proposer opts for a voluntary deductible of ₹5,000 on his private car in addition to the compulsory deductible. The discount on OD premium is:
e: Voluntary deductible discounts for private cars are: ₹2,500 – 20% (max ₹750); ₹5,000 – 25% (max ₹1,500); ₹7,500 – 30% (max ₹2,000); ₹15,000 – 35% (max ₹2,500).

topic: Underwriting and Rating
t: Which of the following cities falls in Zone A for private car own damage rating?
e: Zone A comprises Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, New Delhi and Pune; the rest of India is Zone B. Commercial vehicles are rated in three zones.

topic: Underwriting and Rating
t: Extension of the geographical area of a private car policy to Nepal and Bhutan (IMT-1) requires an additional premium of:
e: IMT-1 extends cover to Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Maldives at ₹500 per vehicle for private cars and commercial vehicles and ₹100 for two-wheelers, covering OD and liability together.

topic: Underwriting and Rating
t: A car fitted with a CNG kit worth ₹50,000 (not factory fitted) is insured. The additional premium for the kit is:
e: The bi-fuel kit is covered by endorsement at 4% of its value for OD (₹2,000 on ₹50,000) plus a flat ₹60 towards the increased third party liability risk.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: An appeal against an award of a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal lies to the High Court under Section 173 within:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 173 allows appeal to the High Court within 90 days of the award. No appeal lies if the amount in dispute is less than ₹1 lakh, and the appellant must deposit ₹25,000 or 50% of the award, whichever is less.

topic: Underwriting and Rating
t: Where the insured has falsely declared his NCB entitlement in the proposal form, the consequence under the policy is:
o: The policy becomes void from inception
Only the NCB discount is recovered with interest
The insurer must still pay the claim and recover the NCB
All benefits under the own damage section are forfeited, though third party cover continues
e: The NCB declaration is a warranty: a false declaration forfeits all benefits under Section I (own damage). Third party cover cannot be avoided against claimants because it is statutory.

topic: Underwriting and Rating
t: The OD premium on a 4.5-year-old private car with ex-showroom price ₹8,00,000 is to be calculated. What IDV should be used?
e: For age exceeding 4 years but not exceeding 5 years, depreciation is 50%. IDV = ₹8,00,000 − 50% = ₹4,00,000.

topic: Policy Documents, Terms and Conditions
t: Under the 'Drivers' clause of the Indian motor policy, a person holding a learner's licence may drive the insured vehicle provided:
o: He is accompanied by a person holding an effective driving licence and sits beside him
He is above 25 years of age
He drives only within city limits
e: The policy covers any person including the insured who holds an effective driving licence, and a learner's licence holder provided he complies with the Central Motor Vehicles Rules on being accompanied by a licensed driver.

topic: Policy Documents, Terms and Conditions
t: Which of the following is NOT a 'General Exception' under the Indian motor package policy?
o: Loss while the vehicle is used outside the geographical area
Liability assumed under a contract which would not have attached otherwise
Loss caused by riot and strike
Loss arising from nuclear weapons material
e: Riot, strike and malicious damage are covered perils under Section I. General exceptions include use outside the geographical area, contractual liability, war and nuclear perils, use not as per limitations as to use and driving by an unlicensed person.

topic: Policy Documents, Terms and Conditions
t: The transfer fee payable to the insurer when a package policy is transferred to the new owner of the vehicle is:
e: The transferee must apply within 14 days of transfer with a fee of ₹50 for transfer of the package policy; the NCB of the previous owner is not transferable to the buyer.

topic: Policy Documents, Terms and Conditions
t: Under the two-wheeler package policy, the compulsory deductible is:
e: Two-wheelers carry a compulsory deductible of ₹100 per claim, compared to ₹1,000 or ₹2,000 for private cars depending on cubic capacity.

topic: Policy Documents, Terms and Conditions
t: The insured sells his car but does not inform the insurer. Three months later the buyer meets with an accident injuring a pedestrian. Which statement is correct?
o: The insurer remains liable to the third party under Section 157, as the certificate is deemed transferred with the vehicle
The insurer is not liable because the policy was never transferred
The buyer must pay the compensation personally
The seller must pay since he is still the insured
e: Section 157 deems the certificate and policy to be transferred to the new owner from the date of transfer, so third party liability continues. Own damage benefits, however, require a formal transfer with the insurer's consent.

topic: Introduction to Motor Insurance
t: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 came into force on:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 1988 Act, which repealed the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, was brought into force on 1 July 1989. The 1939 Act's compulsory insurance chapter had become effective on 1 July 1946.

topic: Policy Documents, Terms and Conditions
t: The 'Notice of claim' condition in the motor policy requires the insured to:
o: Inform the insurer in writing immediately upon the occurrence of any accidental loss or damage, and inform the police immediately in case of theft
Inform the insurer only if the claim exceeds the deductible
e: Immediate written notice to the insurer and, for theft or criminal acts, immediate notice to the police are policy conditions, enabling prompt survey and investigation.

topic: Own Damage Claims and Surveyors
t: A surveyor is appointed to assess an accident claim. Which of the following is NOT ordinarily part of the surveyor's work?
o: Verifying the cause of loss and policy coverage
Assessing the cost of repair/replacement after applying depreciation
Checking the vehicle's registration, licence and permit particulars
Deciding the compensation payable to an injured third party
e: The surveyor assesses own damage loss and reports on coverage, documents and salvage; third party compensation is determined by the Claims Tribunal or settled by the insurer's claims department.

topic: Own Damage Claims and Surveyors
t: Under the IRDAI Master Circular on General Insurance Business (2024), once the final survey report is received, the insurer must decide the claim within:
e: The 2024 master circular requires the survey report within 15 days of appointment and the insurer's decision within 7 days of receiving it, replacing the earlier 30-day norms under the 2017 regulations.

topic: Own Damage Claims and Surveyors
t: In a partial loss claim, 'salvage' of replaced parts:
o: Belongs to the insurer, and its value is deducted from the claim if the insured retains it
Is given to the surveyor as fee
e: Once the insurer pays for replacement, the damaged parts are the insurer's salvage; in practice their assessed value is deducted from the claim when the insured or garage retains them.

topic: Own Damage Claims and Surveyors
t: A 3.5-year-old car's accident repair involves: metal parts ₹80,000, airbags ₹30,000, windscreen ₹12,000, labour ₹15,000. Compulsory deductible ₹2,000. Claim payable is:
e: Metal parts at 25% depreciation (3–4 years): ₹60,000; airbags 50%: ₹15,000; windscreen nil: ₹12,000; labour ₹15,000. Total ₹1,02,000 less ₹2,000 deductible = ₹1,00,000.

topic: Own Damage Claims and Surveyors
t: In a stolen-and-untraced vehicle claim, Form 35 required by the insurer relates to:
e: Form 35 is the notice of termination of hire-purchase, lease or hypothecation agreement, needed so the vehicle can be transferred free of the financier's charge. Forms 29 and 30 deal with transfer of ownership.

topic: Own Damage Claims and Surveyors
t: Under non-standard claim settlement guidelines, where the insured has under-declared the licensed carrying capacity of a commercial vehicle, the deduction from the claim is:
o: Three times the difference in premium
e: For under-declaration of licensed carrying capacity, insurers deduct three times the difference between the premium charged and the premium that should have been charged; other breaches attract settlement at 75%.

topic: Own Damage Claims and Surveyors
t: A car with IDV ₹4,00,000 is stolen. Three weeks later, before settlement, it is recovered with damage of ₹60,000. How is the claim settled?
o: As a partial loss for the accidental damage of ₹60,000 subject to depreciation and deductible
Claim is rejected because the vehicle was recovered
As a total loss with salvage deducted
e: Since the vehicle is traced before settlement, the loss is confined to the damage sustained, which is settled as a partial loss under the policy terms. A total loss settlement arises only if the vehicle remains untraced.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: In United India Insurance v. Tilak Singh (2006), the Supreme Court held that under an Act-only policy on a two-wheeler:
o: The pillion rider carried gratuitously is covered as a third party
The insurer must pay 50% of the award
The pillion rider can claim only under the PA section
The insurer is not liable for a gratuitous pillion rider as the Act does not require such cover
e: The Court held that an Act-only policy need not cover a gratuitous pillion rider; insurers are liable for such passengers only where the policy is extended by payment of premium (for example a package policy with the relevant liability extension).

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: The conventional heads of compensation fixed in Pranay Sethi (2017) are: loss of estate, funeral expenses and loss of consortium at:
e: Pranay Sethi fixed ₹15,000 each for loss of estate and funeral expenses and ₹40,000 for loss of consortium, to be enhanced by 10% every three years.

topic: Fire – standard products
t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Tribunal may permit the insurer to contest the claim on all grounds available to the insured when:
o: There is collusion between the claimant and the insured, or the insured fails to contest the claim
The insurer requests it in writing
e: Section 170 lets the Tribunal, for reasons recorded in writing, implead the insurer to contest on merits where it is satisfied of collusion or the insured's failure to contest; otherwise the insurer is confined to Section 150 defences.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Sarla Verma, where the deceased was a bachelor, the deduction towards personal and living expenses is normally:
e: For a bachelor, 50% is deducted; for a married person the deduction is one-third (2–3 dependants), one-fourth (4–6 dependants) or one-fifth (more than 6 dependants).

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: A claimant settles a motor accident claim at a Lok Adalat. Which statement is correct?
o: The award can be appealed to the High Court within 90 days
The insurer must pay interest at 12% on the award
The settlement needs ratification by IRDAI
The award is deemed a decree of a civil court, is final and no appeal lies
e: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, a Lok Adalat award is deemed a decree of a civil court and is final and binding; it cannot be appealed. Insurers use Lok Adalats to settle TP claims faster and at lower cost.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Section 171 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Claims Tribunal may direct that:
o: The insurer be fined for delay
Compound interest be paid at bank rate
Simple interest be paid on the compensation from the date of the claim at a rate it considers appropriate
No interest is payable on compensation
e: Section 171 empowers the Tribunal to award simple interest at a specified rate from a date not earlier than the date of the claim; Tribunals commonly award around 7.5–9%.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a Claims Tribunal award of ₹80,000 is made against an insurer. Can the insurer appeal to the High Court under Section 173?
o: No, because the amount in dispute is less than ₹1 lakh
e: Section 173(2) bars appeals where the amount in dispute is less than ₹1 lakh (raised from ₹10,000 by the 2019 amendment). The pre-deposit rule applies only where an appeal is maintainable.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: The 'NCB Protection' add-on allows the insured to:
o: Retain the earned NCB even after making a specified number of claims during the policy year
Receive NCB on third party premium
Transfer NCB to any other person
e: NCB protection preserves the accumulated bonus despite one or two claims in the year, subject to conditions; without it, any OD claim resets the NCB to zero at renewal.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: A 'Roadside Assistance' add-on typically provides:
o: Reimbursement of accidental repair without depreciation
Compensation for loss of personal belongings
Services such as towing, flat tyre help, battery jump-start, fuel delivery and locksmith assistance on breakdown
e: Roadside assistance is a service-based add-on for breakdown situations rather than accident indemnity. Nil depreciation, personal belongings and legal expense covers are separate add-ons.

topic: Insurance Act 1938 – key sections
t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938, a life insurance policy cannot be called in question on any ground after how many years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The 2015 amendment made the three-year bar absolute: after three years no policy may be questioned on any ground, including fraud.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: Which of the following is correct regarding long-term motor policies for new private cars in India?
o: Third party cover must be taken for 3 years at the time of sale of a new car
Own damage cover must be taken for 5 years
No long-term policy is permitted for cars
Third party cover must be for 5 years for new cars
e: Since 1 September 2018, new private cars must carry 3-year TP cover and new two-wheelers 5-year TP cover. OD may be annual or long-term as permitted by IRDAI from time to time.

topic: Grievance Redressal, Fraud and Technology
t: An Insurance Ombudsman's award is:
o: Binding on the insurer, which must comply within 30 days of receipt of the award
Binding on both parties and appealable to the High Court
Binding only if the insured is a senior citizen
e: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 the award binds the insurer, which must comply within 30 days and inform the Ombudsman; the complainant is free to pursue other remedies if dissatisfied.

topic: Grievance Redressal, Fraud and Technology
t: Which of the following is an example of 'application fraud' in motor insurance?
o: Inflating the repair bill after an accident
Obtaining a policy with a backdated cover note after the accident has occurred
e: Application (underwriting) fraud occurs at inception, e.g. arranging cover after the loss, misdeclaring NCB or the vehicle's use. Inflated bills are claims fraud; overloading and unlicensed driving are breaches of conditions.

topic: Grievance Redressal, Fraud and Technology
t: The Bima Bharosa portal of IRDAI is:
o: A platform to buy motor policies online
The integrated grievance management system through which policyholders lodge and track complaints against insurers
A tool to compute third party premium
e: Bima Bharosa (earlier IGMS) is IRDAI's online grievance platform that routes complaints to insurers and monitors their resolution within prescribed timelines.
